newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia accepts Singapore leader's apology-report.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia accepts Singapore leader's apology-report.

text.p: The Malaysian Cabinet on Wednesday accepted Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's apology and retraction of disparaging remarks about a Malaysian state, the national news agency Bernama reported.

The acceptance appears to put to rest one of the worst diplomatic rows in years between two countries who were once united as British colonies but who are competing fiercely for regional economic power and influence.
Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi was to hold a news conference at 1600 local time (0800 gmt) to explain the cabinet decision, a foreign ministry spokesman said.
Lee said in a statement on Monday he would ask a local court to delete a remark in an affidavit that the Malaysian state of Johor "was notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

That move followed a rare public apology by the 73-year-old Lee, who led the fight for Singapore's independence and was its prime minister from 1959 until 1990. He now has an elder statesman's role as senior minister.

Lee's remarks infuriated Kuala Lumpur -- which is sensitive to any perceived slurs from its traditionally more economically developed neighbour -- and last week the Foreign Ministry demanded an apology and a retraction.
The controversial remarks were part of an affidavit Lee made in court on January 27 in his libel suit against opposition politician Tang Liang Hong.

Tang fled to Johor Baru, capital of Johor state, immediately after losing a race for parliament in Singapore's general elections on January 2, saying he had received death threats in Singapore. Lee questioned why he would feel safer in Johor.

The predominantly Chinese city state of Singapore and Malaysia were united in the Malaysia Federation from 1963 to 1965 before Singapore was expelled, in part for opposing state policies favouring special rights for ethnic Malays.
